title: Predictive prefetch and client fallthrough — PRD sketch
content:
Status: draft — exploratory PRD with rough API sketches and rollout ideas.

Summary:
We propose a predictive prefetch feature for the Hosted API that reduces end-to-end perceived latency for common tool-calling and structured-output flows by speculatively pre-warming compute, KV prefixes, and (optionally) tool results. The server-side prefetch decisions are guided by lightweight client-provided hints and live telemetry; the SDK offers ergonomics to opt into different predictive strategies and graceful client fallthroughs when predictions are incorrect.

Why this now / problem statement:
- Many customers report tail latency spikes when a call triggers a new model variant or a tool (search, database lookup, code execution) that requires additional round-trips.
- Streaming UX is sensitive: perceived latency for first substantive tokens determines whether a user feels the system is snappy.
- Current fallback patterns are blunt: either block until a full compute path is available or immediately fallback to a lower-fidelity model with no intermediate quality signals.
- Operators want a knob that improves 95–99th percentile latency without wholesale increases in committed capacity.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce median time-to-first-substantive-token by 20–40% for tool-heavy flows on integration customers (A/B test).
- Reduce 95th percentile latency by 15% for sequences that trigger tool calling or model variant fallback.
- Limit additional compute cost to <7% for workloads where predictive prefetch is enabled.
- Provide SDK ergonomics so product teams can opt-in with low lift and can reason about correctness and safety of predictions.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not propose changing compilation/runtime kernel selection logic other than exposing telemetry signals used for selection.
- Not intended to create a fully autonomous prefetcher that ignores client hints; policy must be transparent and controllable.

User stories:
- As a product engineer building a chat assistant that calls a trusted search tool, I want the assistant to start streaming the explanation quickly even when the search call might take 300–400ms behind the scenes.
- As a platform engineer, I want telemetry that shows how often predictive prefetches succeed vs cause wasted compute so I can set policies and budgets.
- As an SRE, I want prefetch traffic to be rate-limited per-tenant and gracefully throttled when capacity is constrained.

Design overview (high-level):
1) Client hints + heuristic model (server-side): clients may send an optional small hint blob (predictive_hint) with an inference request. The blob contains structured flags: likely_tool_call: [none|search|code|db], expected_max_tokens_before_tool (int), confidence_score (0-1), and output_schema_hash (optional). The server merges hints with recent per-tenant telemetry + a lightweight predictive model to decide whether to pre-warm a computation path.

2) Prefetch actions (examples):
- KV prefix pre-warm: populate KV cache for known prompt prefixes that will likely be needed within N tokens.
- Model variant warm: allocate and pin a minimal serving context for a short window if a higher-cost variant is predicted.
- Tool warm: for verified partner tools, optionally issue a prefetch request (e.g., warm a search index query or warm a DB connection pool). For safety, this requires explicit tenant opt-in and per-tool allowlist.

3) Streaming handshake changes (backwards-compatible):
- Extend existing stream start response to include prefetch_status: [none|started|skipped|failed] and predicted_actions list (strings). Clients can display a 'loading' micro-interaction while prefetch is ongoing.
- If prediction is wrong, server emits a correction event in-stream (prefetch_cancellation) so clients can adjust expectation.

4) SDK ergonomics (JS/Python):
- Opt-in flag at call site: {predictive: {mode: "conservative" | "aggressive" | "off", allow_tool_warm: boolean}}
- Telemetry hook: client SDK exposes an event 'prefetchOutcome' with payload {prediction, action, cost_estimate, success:true/false} that apps can surface to internal dashboards.
- Idempotent fallback helpers: SDK includes utilities to manage optimistic UI updates and rollback when prefetch fails. Example pseudo: 
  const resp = await Redwood.createCompletion({prompt, predictive:{mode:'conservative', allow_tool_warm:false}})
  stream.on('prefetchOutcome', (o) => record('prefetch', o))

5) Safety and cost controls:
- Tenant-level budget: predictive prefetch consumes a named budget. If budget exhausted, prefetch decisions degrade to conservative/no prefetch.
- Tool allowlist & privacy: any server-initiated tool prefetching only allowed for tools that explicitly permit prefetching in their integration contract and after tenant grants permission.
- Rate limiting: token-based and RPS-based gating to avoid prefetch storms during traffic spikes.

Acceptance criteria / launch metrics:
- API: stable optional predictive_hint parameter accepted by hosted-api and documented in SDKs.
- Telemetry: dashboard tile showing prefetch attempts, success rate, additional cost, and latency delta.
- A/B test: a 10k-user controlled experiment showing median time-to-first-substantive-token reduced by >=20% in aggressive mode for a targeted use-case (search+explain).
- Fail-safes validated: when prefetch budget disabled, no speculative compute is charged.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (internal): prototype server-side predictor and SDK opt-in in a staging cluster with a few internal demo apps.
- Phase 1 (alpha): invite 3 trusted customers, restrict tool prefetch to allowlist, collect telemetry for 4 weeks.
- Phase 2 (beta): expand to usage-based beta with an opt-in console toggle and per-tenant budget default.
- Phase 3 (general): public SDK release, docs, and default conservative policy (off by default).

Open questions / risks (to resolve before beta):
- Predictive model features: what exact telemetry window should be used for per-tenant heuristics (1h vs 24h)? impact on freshness.
- How to price prefetch compute that does not produce output? Do we bill prefetch attempts differently?
- UX: how should clients indicate speculative content vs confirmed content to end-users (labeling debatable).
- Edge cases: speculative tool results that change user-facing content might be misleading — need strict guidance and opt-in semantics.

Implementation notes / infra needs:
- Lightweight predictor service (stateless scoring) co-located with router layer to keep decisions under 5ms latency.
- Short-lived reserved slot allocation path in serving runtime for model warm actions.
- Console controls: per-tenant toggle, budget slider, allowlist management UI.
- SDK changes: small API additions and telemetry events; ensure backward compatibility.

Engineering ask (rough):
- 2 FE engineers for SDK + console toggles (2 months)
- 3 backend engineers for predictor + router integration + prefetch budget (3 months)
- 2 infra/SRE engineers to extend runtime warm path and capacity gating (2 months)
- 1 research/ML engineer to prototype predictor features (1-2 months)

Notes to reviewers / next steps:
- Review privacy/partner agreements for tool prefetching; any partner tools with paid queries require contractual opt-in.
- Product to validate A/B experiment design with analytics team (metric definitions and instrumentation plan).
- Security: threat modeling for speculative requests that could leak tenant data through tool results — require controls.

Quick sketch of example request (HTTP POST body) for API team:
{
  "prompt": "Find the latest docs on token batching and summarize",
  "stream": true,
  "predictive_hint": {
    "likely_tool_call": "search",
    "expected_max_tokens_before_tool": "60",
    "confidence_score": "0.82",
    "output_schema_hash": "sha256:..."
  },
  "predictive_mode": "conservative"
}

(Implementation will use compact binary hint in production; this JSON is illustrative.)

Appendix — allowed prefetch actions (initial shortlist):
- no-op (explicit skip), kv_prefetch_prefix, model_variant_warm, tool_connection_warm, tool_query_prefetch (opt-in), connection_pool_increase.

I want focused feedback on:
- Is the proposed client hint shape sufficient and safe?
- Policy defaults: should conservative be default-on in SDK or default-off?
- Billing model preference: bill prefetch separately or include in token counts?

End of draft.

Notes-to-self: follow up with GH PR 1427 to include telemetry schema, and align with rollout engineering doc in Confluence.
